Care standards for quiet corners
The purpose of this section is to describe how the desk handles it

Quiet corners are used for travelers and pets that need lower noise, less movement, and a steadier pace at the counter. Staff keep the area clear, keep voices even, and avoid crowding the space with bags, forms, or stray equipment. The senior coordinator oversees daily service choices and sets the order of work when more than one request arrives at once. The desk gives priority to calm handling, clean surfaces, and a direct path to support services when a pet or traveler shows signs of stress.

The companion animal review starts with a basic check of travel papers, carrier condition, and visible comfort needs. Staff note any signs of heat, fear, injury, or poor fit, then pass concerns to the safety coordinator without delay. The safety coordinator reviews hazards and prevention, including floor condition, door movement, nearby noise, and any item that could disturb a pet. If a traveler asks for a quieter spot, the desk will place the matter into the calm review flow and avoid rushed handling.

When service must be paused, staff explain the reason in plain terms and keep the exchange brief. If the matter is simple, the desk resolves it at once. If the matter grows beyond routine support, the senior coordinator steps in and the record is updated in the same visit. Staff do not argue, guess, or move a pet without consent and a clear service need. If a pet like Rosie is involved, the same care rules apply with steady tone and careful spacing.

For help with any unclear case, contact the senior coordinator or the safety coordinator through the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
